B.depoimento: We are launching our first major assault by sending all 12 of our troops from Barcelona to capture the neutral village of Tarragona. At the same time, we are training 2 spearmen in our capital to ensure we maintain a defensive presence while our main force is on the march.
B.plano: Capture the neutral village of Tarragona [21] with our entire current army to secure a second village and start expanding. Build 2 spearmen at Barcelona to leave a defensive garrison at home. Next turn, check the battle outcome and plan the next march, possibly towards Zaragoza [17].

A.depoimento:
I ordered a double attack on the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora, splitting my forces to conquer both simultaneously.
In Lisboa, I built a knight and an archer to prepare for the next phase of expansion.
Securing these villages will give me a strong foothold in the region.
A.plano:
Attack Santarem and Evora with split forces to expand my territory.
Build 1 knight and 1 archer in Lisboa to reinforce the army for next turn.
Focus on securing these two villages to increase resource production.
Keep an eye on the unexplored roads to the north and east for future expansion.

B.depoimento: Orders are given to expand our territory. Barcelona builds 2 spearman and marches all 4 to Girona. Tarragona sends 4 spearman to strike Zaragoza, exploiting our counter against their knights. We aim to secure two key neutral villages to boost our economy and military strength.
B.plano: Capture Girona [23] with 4 spearman from Barcelona, and capture Zaragoza [17] with 4 spearman from Tarragona (using the spearman vs knight counter). Build 2 spearman at Barcelona to have enough troops. Next turn, assess the results and prepare to march towards Madrid or Valencia.

A.depoimento: I ordered a coordinated three-way assault on the neutral villages of Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro, deploying the full garrisons of Santarem and Evora. Lisboa sent its available troops to reinforce Santarem, and I built two archers in the capital to prepare for the next wave of expansion.
A.plano: Conquered Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro. Next turn, focus on securing the newly captured villages and expanding further. Check the road network for new paths to unexplored villages. Build more archers in Lisboa to maintain momentum.

B.depoimento: This turn, I am focusing on rapid expansion by capturing both Girona and Castellon simultaneously. I am reinforcing Zaragoza with the remaining troops from Tarragona to create a powerful strike force for the next turn. With luck, we will have 5 villages by the end of this turn and a strong army ready to march on Madrid.
B.plano: Build 2 spearman at Barcelona and 1 archer at Tarragona. Send 4 spearman from Barcelona to capture Girona [23]. Send 2 archers from Tarragona to capture Castellon [18]. Send the rest of Tarragona's troops (1 spearman, 3 archers, 3 knights) to reinforce Zaragoza [17]. Next turn, use the strong Zaragoza garrison to capture Madrid [12] or Huesca [20].

A.depoimento: My armies have conquered Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro. Now I strike at Sevilha with the might of Faro's garrison, while Santarem's troops march to reinforce Coimbra. My smithies work overtime, forging spearmen to ready my villages for the next battles.
A.plano: Attack Sevilha from Faro to expand territory. Reinforce Coimbra from Santarem to prepare for the assault on Porto. Build spearmen in Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to grow my army for the next battles.

B.depoimento: I am launching my main attack on Madrid from Zaragoza, sending all available troops to secure this key neutral village. I am also sending reinforcements from Barcelona and Castellon to Zaragoza to keep it defended after the assault. I am building more troops across my villages to sustain the campaign toward the enemy capital.
B.plano: Conquer Madrid [12] with Zaragoza's full army to expand my territory. Reinforce Zaragoza with Barcelona's spearman and Castellon's archers so it remains a strong hold. Build 2 spearman at Barcelona, 2 archers at Tarragona, and 2 spearman at Zaragoza to prepare for the next attacks. Next turn, focus on building knights and capturing Huesca [20] or Pamplona [19].

A.depoimento: Our forces march on Porto to secure a northern gateway, while the army from Faro prepares to strike Sevilha. We reinforce Coimbra and Faro to hold the line, and expand our military production with knights and spearmen across the realm.
A.plano: Attack Porto from Coimbra to expand our territory northwards and open a path to Vigo. Reinforce Coimbra from Santarem, and Faro from Evora and Badajoz to secure our southern flank ahead of the Sevilha assault. Build knights in Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to maintain a high-mobility core, and spearmen in Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro to bolster our infantry and counter enemy knights.

B.depoimento: Our armies are on the move! Zaragoza's forces marched on Huesca, while Madrid's full army marched on Burgos. Both attacks are expected to succeed. In our cities, workers train new troops: Barcelona builds a knight, Tarragona and Castellon build spearmen, Zaragoza builds spearmen to replenish ranks. We are expanding and growing stronger.
B.plano: This turn we focus on expansion. Zaragoza attacks Huesca with all forces to capture a northern village. Madrid attacks Burgos with its full army. We build at other villages: Barcelona builds a knight for Girona next turn; Tarragona, Castellon, Zaragoza build spearmen to reinforce and replace losses. Watch for enemy movements and defend if needed. We skip Salamanca to keep Madrid's army intact for Burgos.

A.depoimento: This turn we focused on consolidation. We marched archers and knights from Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, and Badajoz to Coimbra to build a powerful northern army. We also sent spearmen and a knight from Faro to Sevilha to strengthen our southern flank. In our villages, we built knights in the north and spearmen in the south to maintain our military strength. We did not attack this turn, allowing our forces to gather.
A.plano: Concentrating forces in Coimbra and Sevilha for upcoming attacks. Building knights in central villages and spearmen in frontier villages. Sending archers and knights to Coimbra, and spearmen and knight to Sevilha. Will attack Porto and Cordoba next turn after reinforcements arrive.

B.depoimento: We attack Girona! Barcelona's army marches north. Reinforcements strengthen Madrid. Our builders work overtime. The expansion continues!
B.plano: Attack Girona with Barcelona's full force to capture it. Reinforce Madrid with troops from Zaragoza and Burgos to secure the west. Build troops everywhere to grow. Next turn, assess Girona outcome and plan next attack (Valencia or Teruel). Avoid sending weak armies to certain death.

A.depoimento: Our armies have marched on Porto, hoping to overwhelm the knight garrison and capture our first new village. In the meantime, our smithies have been busy forging knights in our central strongholds and archers in the south, while spearman reinforcements stream toward the front lines. The strike on Porto is underway, and we await the outcome.
A.plano: Porto attack launched with all Coimbra forces. Reinforcements (2 spear from Badajoz, 1 knight from Santarem) arriving at Coimbra. Knights built in Coimbra/Badajoz/Faro for Toledo/Salamanca. Sevilha massing 13 troops but needs archers for Cordoba. Next turn: attack Toledo from Badajoz with knights; build more archers in Sevilha; consider Salamanca from Coimbra with knights.

B.depoimento: I ordered the full garrison of Castellon to march on Valencia to secure our first neutral village. Meanwhile, I commanded all other loyal villages to produce troops at maximum capacity to rebuild our forces.
B.plano: Attack Valencia with Castellon's full force to conquer it. Build troops in all possible villages to grow our army. Next turn, assess the outcome and plan the next attack towards Murcia or Teruel.

A.depoimento: Our armies struck three neutrals at once! Porto's knights and archers crushed Salamanca, while its spearmen overwhelmed Vigo. Sevilha's archers and knight conquered Cordoba. We built knights across our realm and sent reinforcements to Badajoz, ready to strike Toledo next turn. The path to Madrid opens through Salamanca!
A.plano: Next turn: attack Toledo from Badajoz with the gathered knights (including those from Faro). Explore Madrid from Salamanca. Consider attacking Murcia from Cordoba. Remember the arriving reinforcements: 2 spear to Coimbra, 2 spear + 1 archer to Sevilha. Keep some troops in Porto and Faro for defense.

B.depoimento: Turn 8 is upon us. Our Valencia conquest is secure, and we now launch a double pronged attack on the neutral villages of Teruel and Pamplona to expand our territory. We have maximized our production of knights and spearmen to ensure victory on the battlefield and secure our path to dominance.
B.plano: We will attack Teruel with 2 knights from Zaragoza and Pamplona with 3 spearmen and 1 knight from Burgos. We build knights in Barcelona, Tarragona, Castellon, Huesca, Madrid, Zaragoza, and spearmen in Girona, Burgos to grow our army. Next turn, we will assess the outcomes of these attacks and plan further expansion towards Murcia, Vigo, or Salamanca.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered our armies to attack the neutral village of Pamplona from Zaragoza and the enemy village of Salamanca from Madrid. I also focused on building knights across my territory to strengthen our forces. We are making steady progress towards our goal of holding 18 villages.
B.plano: We successfully conquered Pamplona and Salamanca this turn, bringing our total to 11 villages. We built knights in almost all our villages to grow our army. Next turn, we will assess the situation, look for new neutral or enemy villages to attack, and continue our expansion towards 18 villages.

A.depoimento: The loss of Salamanca was a setback, but we will not let it stand. I have ordered the knights from Badajoz to ride hard and assault Salamanca. Our tactical advantage should see us through, and we will reclaim our land. All other garrisons are building up, ready to strike next turn.
A.plano: Our main objective this turn is to reclaim Salamanca. I am sending all 4 knights from Badajoz to attack Salamanca. The knight counter against their spearman should give us a decisive advantage. Coimbra will remain on high defense with its 4 spearman to protect our flank. All other villages are building a mix of spearman, archers, and knights to prepare for the next wave of expansions towards Toledo and Madrid.

B.depoimento: We launched a decisive attack this turn, splitting our forces in Salamanca to conquer the empty village of Porto and the enemy-held Badajoz. At the same time, we are reinforcing Pamplona to secure our northern border and building up our army with knights across our villages.
B.plano: This turn we focus on expanding our territory by attacking Porto and Badajoz from Salamanca, while reinforcing Pamplona which our marching army will conquer next turn. We build knights in almost all our villages to grow our army. Next turn, we will assess the battle results, consolidate our new territories, and plan the next phase of our expansion towards 18 villages.

A.depoimento: We launched a coordinated double strike this turn, sending our knights from Salamanca to attack Madrid, while a spearman-heavy force from Vigo assaulted Burgos. At the same time, we began a massive reinforcement movement, sending troops from our interior villages to the front lines to secure our newly conquered territories and prepare for further advances.
A.plano: We are launching a double attack on Madrid (from Salamanca) and Burgos (from Vigo) to secure our northern border. We are reinforcing all our border villages with troops from the interior (Porto to Vigo, Coimbra to Salamanca, Sevilha to Cordoba, Lisboa to Santarem, Santarem to Badajoz, Evora to Faro) to prepare for the next wave of expansions. Every village is building 1 knight to grow our army.

B.depoimento: We launched a two-pronged attack on Salamanca and Teruel while reinforcing our vulnerable borders. Madrid sent its knights to take the weakly held Salamanca, while Castellon's knights struck at the neutral Teruel. Reinforcements poured into Madrid and Burgos from nearby villages to deter enemy counterattacks. Our builders worked overtime, churning out knights in nearly every village to swell our ranks for the next push.
B.plano: Attack Salamanca (2 knights from Madrid) and Teruel (3 knights from Castellon). Reinforce Madrid with knights from Barcelona (3), Tarragona (2), Zaragoza (1). Reinforce Burgos with knights from Pamplona (3). Send 2 spear/2 archer from Valencia to Castellon, 3 spear from Huesca to Pamplona. Build knights in all possible villages. Next turn: consolidate Salamanca and Teruel, plan attacks on Badajoz and Vigo, explore unexplored.

A.depoimento: Our armies conquer Toledo and Murcia. Knights ride to strengthen our border castles. The forges of the interior villages work without cease.
A.plano: We are attacking the neutral villages Toledo and Murcia to increase our territory to 14. We are sending knights to reinforce Salamanca and Burgos, preparing for attacks on Madrid and Pamplona next turn. We are building spearmen and archers to grow our army. Watch for enemy counterattacks.

B.depoimento: King B orders the storming of Toledo with the Madrid garrison, crushing their archers with our knights. We reinforce Valencia for the next push south, and shuffle our northern and interior forces to the borders. The army grows strong for the campaign to come!
B.plano: Conquer Toledo with 6 knights from Madrid. Reinforce Valencia from Castellon to prepare for Murcia. Move troops from Tarragona to Zaragoza and Huesca to Pamplona to strengthen the northern front. Build knights in all major villages to grow the army.

A.depoimento: We launched a powerful knight assault from Salamanca on Madrid, aiming to crush the enemy garrison and expand our territory. Simultaneously, we reinforced our border villages of Cordoba, Badajoz, and Burgos, while our home villages worked tirelessly to produce more spearman and knights for the coming campaigns.
A.plano: Attack Madrid with 8 knights from Salamanca to conquer it. Reinforce Cordoba, Badajoz, and Burgos with spearman from Sevilha and Vigo. Build a mix of spearman and knights in all villages to maintain troop production for the next attacks on Toledo and Pamplona.

B.depoimento: My armies strike on all fronts! Toledo's knights take Cordoba, Pamplona's forces crush Burgos, and Valencia's troops conquer Murcia. Zaragoza reinforces Madrid, Castellon reinforces Valencia. I am building knights and archers everywhere. The path to 18 villages is underway!
B.plano: Conquer Cordoba, Burgos, and Murcia this turn. Reinforce Madrid from Zaragoza and Valencia from Castellon. Build knights and archers to grow the army. Next turn, assess losses and prepare for Salamanca and Badajoz.

A.depoimento: My armies conquered Madrid and Cordoba last turn, and now I am striking at Toledo and Zaragoza to expand my territory. I am reinforcing my border villages to hold the gains and building troops for the next phase of the campaign.
A.plano: Attack Toledo and Zaragoza to secure the border and increase my village count to 16. Reinforce Madrid, Cordoba, and Burgos to hold the newly conquered territories. Build a mix of knights and archers in all villages to prepare for the next attacks on Pamplona and Valencia.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch a decisive attack on Murcia from Valencia, leveraging our numerical superiority. We reinforce Toledo and Zaragoza to prepare for the next phase of our campaign against Cordoba and Madrid. Our builders work tirelessly to produce archers and knights, strengthening our core villages. We aim to expand our territory and secure the path to victory.
B.plano: Focus on the southern and eastern fronts. Attack Murcia from Valencia with all available troops. Reinforce Toledo from Teruel to prepare for the attack on Cordoba next turn. Reinforce Zaragoza from Tarragona and Huesca to prepare for the attack on Madrid. Build archers and knights in all villages to grow the army and replenish losses. Do not attack Burgos yet as it is too strong.

B.depoimento: Turn 16: I am launching a double attack on the southern front. My armies from Murcia and Toledo will strike Cordoba and Badajoz respectively, aiming to conquer both villages and open the path to the unexplored south. Meanwhile, I am reinforcing Zaragoza to secure the northern border and prepare for the next push towards Madrid. My factories are working overtime, building archers and knights to replenish my forces.
B.plano: Focus on the southern front. Attack Cordoba from Murcia and Badajoz from Toledo with most troops, leaving minimal garrisons. Reinforce Zaragoza from Tarragona, Huesca, and Pamplona to prepare for the attack on Madrid next turn. Build archers and knights in all villages to grow the army. Do not attack Burgos yet.

A.depoimento: This turn we ordered a full assault on Badajoz, sending eight knights from Faro and five from Santarem to overwhelm the enemy garrison. At the same time, we marched reinforcements to our exposed border villages and began rebuilding our army with a balance of knights and archers to counter the enemy's diverse troop types.
A.plano: We are attacking Badajoz with all available knights from Faro and Santarem to reclaim this border village. Reinforcements are being sent to strengthen Santarem, Faro, Salamanca, and Madrid against expected counterattacks. We are building a mix of knights and archers to prepare for attacks on Cordoba and other enemy villages.

B.depoimento: We have conquered Cordoba and Badajoz, securing the southern front. Now we focus on Madrid, the key to the northern enemy territories. Our armies from Zaragoza and Toledo will strike hard. We are also reinforcing our newly gained lands and building up our forces across the realm.
B.plano: Attack Madrid from Zaragoza and Toledo with most troops. Send Murcia's troops to reinforce Cordoba, and Valencia's to Murcia. Send Tarragona's troops to reinforce Zaragoza. Build archers and knights in all villages to grow the army. Do not attack Burgos or Sevilha yet.

B.depoimento: I launched a decisive attack on Sevilha with Cordoba's entire army, aiming to break the southern front. Simultaneously, I reinforced Madrid and shifted troops to Toledo to shore up its weak defenses. My builds focus on producing archers and knights to maintain momentum. The enemy will struggle to counter all these moves at once.
B.plano: Attack Sevilha with Cordoba's full army to conquer it and break the southern front. Reinforce Madrid with Zaragoza's troops and redirect Madrid's garrison to Toledo to defend against a potential Badajoz assault. Send Murcia's troops to Cordoba to replenish losses. Build troops across all villages to grow the army for the next push after Sevilha falls.

A.depoimento: Our knights stormed Toledo, shattering the enemy defenses and claiming the city for ourselves. Simultaneously, we marched vast reinforcements to our borderlands, fortifying them against enemy counterattacks. The kingdom's armies are on the move, and we will not stop until the enemy's villages fall.
A.plano: We are launching a major offensive on Toledo with 8 knights from Badajoz, aiming to capture this key hub and open the southern front. We are reinforcing Badajoz, Sevilha, Salamanca, and Burgos with troops from interior villages to secure our borders and prepare for subsequent attacks on Cordoba and the north. We are building troops across our territory to sustain the campaign. Next turn, we will assess the battle results and plan the next attacks, likely on Cordoba from our strengthened Sevilha or Toledo.

B.depoimento: Turn 19 is the turning point! I am launching a massive three-pronged attack on the southern and western fronts. Cordoba will take the weakly defended Sevilha, Toledo will storm Badajoz, and Madrid will assault Salamanca. Simultaneously, I am sending reinforcements from the interior to secure the borders and building a new generation of knights and archers to ensure our army grows stronger than ever. The enemy will not know what hit them!
B.plano: Launch a triple offensive on Sevilha, Badajoz, and Salamanca to secure key territories and shift the borders. Send Cordoba's army to Sevilha, Toledo's to Badajoz, and Madrid's to Salamanca, leaving minimal garrisons but reinforcing them with Zaragoza, Teruel, and Murcia. Build troops across all villages, focusing on knights where iron is abundant and spearmen/archers elsewhere, to prepare for the next wave of expansions.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies struck at Madrid, overwhelming the enemy garrison. We reinforced our border villages and built a mix of knights and archers to counter the enemy's strengths. The path to victory is clear: we will continue our offensive next turn.
A.plano: Attack Madrid from Salamanca to conquer our 13th village. Reinforce Salamanca, Toledo, Sevilha from Badajoz. Build knights and archers to balance our army. Next turn: attack Cordoba from Sevilha and Teruel from Toledo.
